content: We do not inherit the earth from our ancestors; we borrow it from our children.
author: Native American Proverbs
explanation: Modern consumption views the soil, waters, and forests as an inheritance to be exploited and spent for immediate gratification. Indigenous wisdom inverts this arrogance: we are merely temporary caretakers of a sacred trust that belongs to the unborn children who will walk these trails after us.
practicalInsight: Make one choice today that treads lightly on the earth—conserve water, eliminate waste, or protect living soil.
reflectionPrompt: Are you living as an owner who consumes the earth, or as a loving trustee preserving it for your children?
